question: What does Gross National Product measure in a national economy?

options.A: Total money spent strictly on public and private hospitals
options.B: Total value of goods and services produced by country residents
options.C: Total revenue generated solely from crude oil exportation
options.D: Total amount of foreign debt accumulated by the government

explanation: GNP calculates the economic output generated by a country's citizens and businesses both domestically and abroad. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why does a high Gross National Product fail to guarantee adequate healthcare funding?

options.A: Political priorities and policy decisions determine sector budget allocation
options.B: National wealth is automatically distributed entirely to the agricultural sector
options.C: International monetary funds strictly prohibit spending on public health
options.D: Hospitals are legally barred from receiving funds from national production

explanation: An economy can produce massive wealth, but the government decides through budgets how much of that wealth actually reaches health services. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h1)

question: What does health expenditure as a percentage of GNP calculate?

options.A: The exact profit margin made by private pharmaceutical companies
options.B: The proportion of national economic output dedicated to health
options.C: The total taxes paid exclusively by registered nurses and doctors
options.D: The ratio of international loans given to build federal hospitals

explanation: This metric reveals what exact fraction of the country's total wealth production goes into running health services. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is a major consequence of a low percentage of GNP allocated to health?

options.A: Excessive availability of free medications in rural clinics
options.B: Immediate reduction in the training duration for student nurses
options.C: Heavy reliance on out-of-pocket spending by poor patients
options.D: Complete elimination of private health insurance companies

explanation: When governments invest a tiny fraction of national wealth into health, citizens must pay for their own care directly at the point of service. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h2)

question: What minimum percentage of national budgets did the Abuja Declaration recommend for health?
explanation: African leaders signed the Abuja Declaration committing to allocate at least fifteen percent of their annual budgets to healthcare development. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why do international health agencies constantly track adherence to the Abuja Declaration targets?

options.A: To regulate the market prices of imported medical diagnostic equipment
options.B: To measure government commitment and hold leaders accountable for underfunding
options.C: To determine which countries qualify for mandatory military protection
options.D: To calculate the exact salaries of nursing tutors across the continent

explanation: Tracking this target shows whether governments are putting enough domestic resources behind their stated public health commitments. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which factor most directly reduces available government revenue for Nigerian health budgets?

options.A: Fluctuations in global crude oil prices
options.B: High public demand for routine immunization services
options.C: Increased international donations from foreign agencies
options.D: Excessive recruitment of entry-level staff nurses

explanation: Nigeria relies heavily on oil revenue, so when global oil prices drop, total government income falls and health allocations shrink. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h4)

question: How does heavy national debt servicing affect healthcare funding in developing economies?

options.A: It forces the government to raise nurses' salaries above standard rates
options.B: It guarantees timely delivery of medical consumables to rural posts
options.C: It leaves very little money available for social sectors like health
options.D: It automatically increases foreign grants for maternal and child care

explanation: When a large chunk of national income goes into paying off debts, fewer financial resources remain for public services like healthcare. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a direct operational result of low health sector funding in public hospitals?

options.A: Chronic shortages of basic medical consumables and supplies
options.B: Instant promotion of all overworked clinical nursing staff
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced diagnostic imaging machines
options.D: Complete elimination of out-of-pocket payments for patients

explanation: Underfunded health sectors lack the financial muscle to regularly purchase basic items like syringes, gloves, and drugs. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h5)

question: How does poor health financing directly affect the working life of a bedside nurse?

options.A: It provides abundant time for nurses to conduct advanced clinical research
options.B: It creates stressful conditions where nurses must improvise care with few resources
options.C: It ensures that nurses receive hazard allowances ahead of all other workers
options.D: It guarantees that every ward has automated patient monitoring systems

explanation: When facilities lack supplies and staff, nurses suffer severe stress trying to save lives under impossible working conditions. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary aim of implementing mandatory social health insurance schemes?

options.A: To ensure that private pharmacies make maximum commercial profits
options.B: To eliminate the need for professional nursing registration exams
options.C: To replace government budgets entirely with private corporate funds
options.D: To reduce catastrophic out-of-pocket spending for ordinary citizens

explanation: Health insurance pools financial risks so that individuals do not face bankruptcy when sudden medical emergencies occur. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h6)

question: How do sin taxes on items like tobacco and alcohol help the health sector?

options.A: They double the monthly salaries of all registered public servants
options.B: They generate dedicated revenue streams to fund healthcare services
options.C: They force private hospitals to lower their admission charges
options.D: They completely eradicate all lifestyle diseases within the population

explanation: Placing taxes on harmful products creates a steady source of income that can be channeled directly into supporting public health. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h6)
